docs.inserted: Some deployment tooling cannot read `poetry.lock` directly. Once `poetry install` has succeeded, write the same pinned set out for it with `poetry export --without-hashes --output requirements.txt`.
docs.why_implied: The passage sequences `poetry install` and then `poetry export` as the next step of the same workflow, with no mention of `poetry self add poetry-plugin-export`. It never says the export command is built in; the reader has to infer that the step is only complete if the Export plugin still shipped with Poetry, which it has not since 2.0. The doc says nothing else about export, so keyword matching on "export" finds only a step that looks ordinary.

docs.inserted:
If you edit a constraint in `pyproject.toml` by hand, bring the lock file back in sync from the project root:

```bash
poetry lock --no-update
```
docs.why_implied: The example uses a flag that no longer exists: `lock` now only accepts `--regenerate`, because not updating already-locked packages became the default. The lead-in makes no claim about what `poetry lock` does; the staleness lives entirely in the removed argument, and seeing it requires knowing that opting out of updates is no longer something you ask for. Searching the doc for the fact's own words ("already been added to the lock file", "will not be updated", "--regenerate") finds nothing - the surrounding section only discusses whether to commit the lock file.

docs.inserted: The environment you activate for this stays in effect until you type `exit`, so leave it again before you run Poetry commands for another project.
docs.why_implied: It describes what the reader will have to do - type `exit` to get out of the activated environment - which is only true of a spawned subshell, i.e. the old `poetry shell`. With `poetry env activate` you eval the printed command in your own shell and leave it with `deactivate`; typing `exit` would close your shell. The sentence never names `poetry shell` or the plugin at all, so no keyword search for the fact's terms can reach it; the contradiction is only visible to a reader who knows how activation works today.

docs.inserted: If you are working on a machine that still has a Poetry 1.x installation, `poetry shell` is available there without installing anything extra.

docs.inserted: Had the `shell` command not been moved out into `poetry-plugin-shell`, users who would rather not work inside a nested shell would have had no way to leave that behaviour out of their installation.
docs.why_implied: Not stale: a counterfactual in the past perfect about what would have happened if the move had not taken place. It presupposes the current fact - `shell` lives in `poetry-plugin-shell` - and asserts nothing false about today's Poetry.
